name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) will be held in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July, bringing together PhD students and young researchers working on all aspects of AI. The program offers introductory and advanced courses, specialized tutorials on bilateral AI and digital humanism, and a rich social programme that includes networking opportunities and a reception at the Vienna City Hall. ESSAI aims to provide a broad view of AI, foster connections between sub‑disciplines, and create a collaborative environment for participants from across Europe and beyond.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC countries and doctoral students, offering technical talks, hands‑on sessions, and discussions on open‑science approaches to multilingual large language models. The event is fully subsidized by the OpenEuroLLM project, includes free bus transfers from Oslo Airport and provides meals and accommodation options in a mountain setting.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The ProbAI 2026 Probabilistic AI School will be held in Vilnius, Lithuania from August 3‑7, 2026. The school aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine‑learning and artificial‑intelligence topics. It welcomes enthusiasts, students, academics, and industry professionals to participate.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a broad range of computer‑vision topics delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme includes daily oral talks, hands‑on labs, and social events such as a dinner and poster reception.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: OxML 2026 offers a summer program to upskill participants in the latest AI theory and applications across three specialised tracks. Learners study with world‑renowned experts from frontier AI labs in both academia and industry, benefiting from a unique and customisable experience. Participants can choose any combination of tracks to match their individual learning goals.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers focusing on robotics, perception, and learning. It covers topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning, and decision making through keynotes, industry talks, brainstorming sessions, and student presentations. Held at the Happy Tammsvik resort in Stockholm, the school aims to foster new collaborations by providing a relaxed setting with indoor and outdoor activities.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI for robotics, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience using state‑of‑the‑art technology. The programme targets master’s‑level students and industry practitioners, providing networking opportunities with academics and industry leaders.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers and professionals, offering intensive lectures by leading experts, hands‑on sessions, and opportunities for scholarships and networking.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems is held at Umeå University in Sweden. It offers lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session and a social program aimed at researchers, students, and professionals interested in the societal implications of AI and AS. The three‑day event (11–13 March 2026) provides networking opportunities and practical experience in ethical AI topics.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The SoRAIM’27 Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia brings together researchers from fields such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing, and human‑robot interaction. Aimed primarily at PhD students and early‑career researchers, the program offers lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking in a mountain setting near Grenoble. The school encourages cross‑disciplinary exchange, collaboration, and provides a broad perspective on social AI and multimedia technologies.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference includes a Winter School held from January 11th to 15th in Tromsø, Norway. It offers intensive training on state-of-the-art deep learning methods such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction, and speech recognition. The school targets researchers and practitioners looking to deepen their expertise and foster collaborations within the international AI community.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an 11‑day intensive program held in Kathmandu, Nepal, featuring AI lectures, labs, and project work. It covers topics from fundamental mathematics and statistics to advanced AI methods such as geometric deep learning, generative modeling, and neuro‑symbolic AI, targeting senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals. The school aims to foster collaboration, provide hands‑on experience, and inspire researchers from Nepal and the broader region to tackle high‑impact AI challenges.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers a series of lectures and tutorials on advanced machine learning topics delivered by leading researchers from institutions such as Google DeepMind, MIT, and the University of Montenegro. The program is aimed at graduate students and early‑career researchers seeking intensive training and networking opportunities in the field of machine learning.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day intensive program that brings together early‑stage researchers and experts to present keynotes, lectures and hands‑on sessions on modern AI topics. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, especially from the Mediterranean region, and encourages participants to showcase their work in poster sessions and to network through social activities. The 2027 edition will be held in Spain in September and covers areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics in machine learning.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI takes place at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers a five‑day immersive program for master, Ph.D., post‑doc, and industry researchers, featuring lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship on state‑of‑the‑art multimodal and generative AI techniques. Organised jointly by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe and Soft Centre, the school aims to build the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco through expert instruction and extensive networking opportunities.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing (AthNLP) Summer School 2026 will be held at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. The program offers intensive lectures and hands‑on sessions on state‑of‑the‑art NLP methods, targeting graduate students and researchers in the field. It is jointly organized by several research institutes and universities, and it precedes the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Chania.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The course provides an intensive introduction to deep unsupervised learning, covering generative AI, clustering, self‑supervised and semi‑supervised methods. It is aimed at STEM students with intermediate AI/ML experience who are considering graduate study or research, and includes both theoretical lectures and practical, real‑world applications. The programme can be taken either residentially or online at Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, offering hands‑on experience with state‑of‑the‑art models.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars in Caen, Normandy, France. It focuses on applying deep‑learning techniques to accelerate scientific research, covering topics such as machine learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations. The program combines lectures with hands‑on Python workshops using libraries like NumPy and PyTorch to give participants practical experience in implementing AI models for scientific problems.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program on the Lappeenranta campus offering courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, and the intersection of business and technology. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students who can earn 3 ECTS credits per course through lectures, workshops, group work and a social programme set in the Finnish summer environment. The programme combines academic learning with hands‑on activities, networking events, and outdoor experiences to inspire participants and showcase Finland’s natural beauty.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: The AIces 2026 International School focuses on the cognitive, ethical and societal dimensions of artificial intelligence. It is aimed at graduate and postgraduate students, as well as industry practitioners, offering parallel courses, a symposium, and open debates. The event takes place in Porto, Portugal from 30 March to 2 April 2026, with both face‑to‑face interaction and live online participation, and recordings available for 45 days after the school.
